description: Localized story-demonstration message rows (STDM_*). Script loading collects message ids by a transformed substring key across the shared GameText tables, and story-demo widgets resolve each id through GetGameTextById.

ID.simple: Story demo message id (row key), e.g. STDM_0100001_0004.
ID.technical: FName ID of FGameDataTableRow_GameText (+0x0, empty default constructor); in all 11 exported language shards the DataTable row key equals the embedded ID, while Properties.ImportKeyField is the differently cased 'Id'. Direct lookup (FindTextRow/GetGameText/HasText/HasGameTextContent) calls UDataTable::FindRow with the requested FName against row names and returns the first hit in the shared TextDataTables array; the embedded ID is read by FindTextIdsContaining. UGameScriptPlayer::UpdateLoad calls GameScript_GetStoryTextId(ScriptAssetId.PrimaryAssetName) and passes the result to AGameTextManager::FindTextIdsContaining. For non-sub-story names that helper first handles the exact STDM_06086B -> STDM_06086A rewrite (case-insensitive comparison), then globally replaces 'A' with '01' and 'B' with '03' using FString::Replace's default case-insensitive search; names containing STDM_SS_ instead replace that token with STDM_00 and append '01'. FindTextIdsContaining scans rows from all 14 language-loaded GameText tables and case-insensitively tests Row->ID.Contains(KeyString), so the key is a substring, not an anchored prefix; returned ids are copied to FGameScriptContext::MessageIdList and sorted. MessageIndex starts at 0 except for script STDM_06086B, where it starts at 40; GetCurrentMessageId returns FName() when the index is out of range, and show commands advance the index per displayed line. Show commands pass the current id to UGameStoryDemoWidget::ShowMessage and separately use the same id as Row->Id in the DLC, short-story, or normal StoryDemoVoice table according to script classification. This table is the eighth of the 14 shared GameText tables (zero-based index 7), with only one language's asset loaded at a time.

Text.simple: Localized story-demo message text; a value can contain embedded newlines that the display parser splits into multiple lines.
Text.technical: FString row text (+0x10, empty default constructor). UGameStoryDemoMultiRichTextBlockWidget::DisplayMessage calls AGameTextManager::GetGameTextById(MessageId), which builds an id-only request in the current language; GetGameText copies Row->Text, returns an empty string when no row is found, and runs FormatText on the copy. FormatText substitutes only GLO (Glossary map) and DYN (request parameter map) tags matching <TYPE=KEY>[MODS], with ABS/RATE_TO_PCT/FULL_WIDTH/HALF_WIDTH/DECIMAL_PLACE_1..4 modifiers, before the widget feeds the result to UGameWidgetMarkupParseProcessor::Parse. Parse splits embedded newlines into lines; DisplayMessage applies the named rich-text style and LineSpace from ShowMessageStyleDataMap, then BuildLineTexts/ApplyLineTexts lay out up to the configured display blocks and reveal characters at the 0.05 s default interval (or immediately when bImmediate is true). None of the 11 exported Text columns contains a '<' character or GLO/DYN tag, so the formatter and markup rules are shared infrastructure rather than observed data in these shards. A missing id resolves to empty text and therefore no parsed lines.

notes: Export check: all 11 shipped shards (De, En, Es, Es_LA, Fr, It, Ja, Ko, Pt, Zh_Hans, Zh_Hant) have 2,469 rows, identical row-key/ID sets, row key == ID, exactly the ID/Text columns, and no empty Text; all IDs match STDM_#######_####. Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45 cooks TextDataTable_<Language> into chunks 1-11. EApplicationLanguage also names Ar, Ind, Pl, Ru and Th, but no matching exports or cook rules were supplied.

Discovery spans every non-null table in AGameTextManager::TextDataTables: Glossary, Battle, Item, CommandList, Chat, Stamp, StoryText, StoryDemo, ShortStoryDemo, Tutorial, BattleSubTitle, Sound, DlcStoryDemoTextDataTable1 and DlcStoryDemoTextDataTable2, all resolved with the current language suffix. The shared array is cleared and rebuilt only after all language loads complete, then OnCultureTextLoaded is broadcast; there is no per-id display cache, although the sequencer tracks DisplayedMessageId to skip a repeated DisplayMessage. In the supplied exports the exact 2,469 StoryDemo IDs are disjoint from the other GameText table IDs, but other shards contain 1,802 different STDM_ IDs, so a script's substring search can legitimately return rows from ShortStoryDemo/DlcStoryDemo tables; of 245 exported Script rows, 154 transformed keys match rows here, 84 only match other GameText shards and 7 match none.

Voice precedence is script-based, not text-table-based: for cue-sheet selection UpdateLoad checks GALLERY_ first (its lookup map has no entries in the reconstruction), then sub-story -> fixed 'Part', then DLC -> DlcStoryDemoVoice, otherwise StoryDemoVoice. ParseVoice skips TimeId == TEXT_TIME_NONE, then checks DLC first, sub-story -> ShortStoryVoice second, and normal -> StoryDemoVoice last; it finds a voice row by exact Row->Id == MessageId and resolves Row->Id_Voice in VoiceDataTables. A StoryDemo text row therefore has no guaranteed voice row, and the text table itself is never consulted for that classification.

Transformed ids and indices are not simple suffixes: A/B are case-insensitively replaced everywhere, STDM_06086B is rewritten to STDM_06086A before that replacement, STDM_SS_* becomes STDM_00* plus '01', STDM_06086B's MessageIndex starts at 40, and UGameStoryDemoWidget::ShowMessage routes by LineId with hard-coded Es_LA overrides for STDM_0303803_0300 and STDM_0608201_0170 instead of using the text id to pick a widget.

Reconstruction evidence: GetGameTextById (0x14af690), GetGameText (0x14af510), HasText (0x14b2ef0), FormatText (0x14c4870), DisplayMessage (0x16867f0) and ShowMessage::Start (0x1444690), and ParseVoice (0x14452a0) are byte-matched. FindTextRow<GameText> (0x14af290, BEHAV NA15) and AGameTextManager::Tick (0x14c96f0, BEHAV BG03) are behaviour-certified rather than byte-identical. FindTextIdsContaining (0x14b0100) is byte-equal in the isolated comparison but HOLD because /OPT:REF removed it from our linked exe; do not describe it as behaviour-certified. Script prefix building (0x1436630), UpdateLoad (0x1440570), ShowMessageBase::Update (0x1438e10), UGameStoryDemoWidget::ShowMessage (0x1686b30) and sequencer show-voice evaluation (0x179f410) are BEHAV-certified. Retail-only Blueprint/asset wiring and absent languages remain unverified.

usages.detail: StartLanguageLoading resolves StoryDemoTextDataTable_<Language> with the other 13 GameText base names and unloads the previous language's loaders.
Tick installs the resolved table as the eighth (zero-based 7) entry of the 14-table TextDataTables array after loads complete.
FindTextIdsContaining scans all GameText rows and returns embedded IDs whose string contains the transformed script key, case-insensitively.
FindTextRow matches an id by DataTable row name and returns the first hit; GetGameText/HasText/HasGameTextContent all route through this shared array.
GameScript_GetStoryTextId transforms the script id into the substring key used for message discovery.
UpdateLoad stores the returned ids in MessageIdList, sorts them, and sets MessageIndex to 0 (or 40 for STDM_06086B).
GetCurrentMessageId reads MessageIdList[MessageIndex] and returns FName() for an out-of-range index.
ShowMessage::Start parses the current id for display and calls ParseVoice; the latter joins the id to DLC, ShortStory, or StoryDemo voice rows according to script classification.
Scheduled show-message entries pass the stored MessageId to UGameStoryDemoWidget::ShowMessage; Decide repeats this on the instant path at line 1270.
ShowMessage finds the target rich-text widget by LineId, with two hard-coded Es_LA message-id overrides, then calls DisplayMessage.
DisplayMessage resolves the id through GetGameTextById, parses the localized string, and applies styles, line layout and character reveal.
Level-sequence ShowMessage sections bypass MessageIdList and call DisplayMessage directly for their FName TextId, guarded by DisplayedMessageId.
The same sequencer section looks up StoryDemoVoice then DlcStoryDemoVoice rows by TextId and plays the resolved voice once.
